source: can you make me a 3d game where a player is fixed to y axis, moving only left or right, with a started weapon that fires at a slow rate. There are 2 lanes in front of them, 1 with enemies and another with walls that provide upgrades. players can choose which to shoot at. if a player cannot kill the enemies in front of them they die

image_prompt.text: Modular two-lane track segments whose exit pivot matches the next segment origin, so the pair of lanes in front of the player extends indefinitely without drift
Lane-crossing objects timed against the approach speed so the player has to choose a target under pressure
Enemies that reach the player end the run - failing to clear the lane in front of you is the death condition
Walls spanning the second lane that the player shoots to gain an upgrade

layout_placement.text: Pickup runs laid along the lanes to bait the player into the riskier one
The upgrade carried by each shootable wall in the second lane - weapon and fire-rate boosts that alter the next stretch of the run

notes: Two lanes, not three. The shape is written around rigid parallel lanes typically numbering three, and the two-lane count has nowhere to live in the emitted block.

The prompt never says whether the world scrolls toward a stationary player or the player advances. It was read as a runner because the player is pinned to one axis and enemies arrive in front of them, but that is an assumption that changes the whole generator.

The player shoots rather than dodges. Infinite Runner supplies the lane geometry but nothing in it expresses a firing position, and Shooter was not loaded because none of its options would have covered it either.

open_questions.ask: Does the world scroll toward the player, or does the player advance down the lanes? That is the difference between a runner and a corridor shooter.
What are the enemies and the setting - sci-fi drones, zombies, cartoon blobs?
Is the run endless with a distance score, or are there finite levels?

coverage_missing.ask: Is forward motion automatic, or is the player stationary while lanes come to them?
What do the enemies and the lanes look like?
Endless run with a score, or discrete levels?

answers.ask: Does the world scroll toward the player, or does the player advance down the lanes? That is the difference between a runner and a corridor shooter.
answers.answer: The world scrolls toward the player; make it a runner-style corridor shooter with the player fixed on the Y axis and only moving left or right.

answers.ask: What are the enemies and the setting - sci-fi drones, zombies, cartoon blobs?
answers.answer: Use a sci-fi setting with enemy drones and upgrade walls.

answers.ask: Is the run endless with a distance score, or are there finite levels?
answers.answer: Use finite, short levels so the game has clear completion points.
